tasks.short: Maintain emergency response plans and procedures

steps.what: Review site changes, emergency routes and response equipment
Discuss response responsibilities and practical changes with site personnel
Record actual response changes and conditions in the revision brief
Revise emergency procedure text to express the agreed changes

loop.input: Existing procedure and specialist-entered change brief with explicit unchanged sections
loop.output: Proposed revisions with each changed instruction linked to the brief
loop.check: Specialist edits in s4 and checks operational meaning, sequence, responsibilities and omissions against site reality in s6
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; unsupported safety instruction or unclear scope means manual revision
loop.why_not_simpler: Use standard procedure sections first; expressing site-specific agreed changes requires prose beyond fixed fields

steps.what: Copy verified response contacts into the revised plan's contact table
Check final procedure meaning, contacts, routes and distribution recipients
Send the checked final emergency plan to its named internal recipients

tasks.design: Use {DOCS} templates for verified contact tables and bounded revision drafting from the specialist's actual change brief. Keep site checks, consultation and full final operational review, then send the exact checked plan through {EMAIL} to its approved internal recipients.
tasks.previous_blocker: Site-specific revision prose was mixed with repeat contact-table assembly and distribution.
tasks.enabler_now: Native templates and bounded change drafting can preserve explicit source references and unchanged sections.
tasks.still_hard: A clear sentence can still specify an impractical or unsafe emergency sequence.
tasks.human_edge: The specialist checks whether real people can execute the procedure under emergency conditions.
tasks.altitude: Less drafting and contact copying; emergency response design and final responsibility stay with the specialist.

reach.task: Verify a response route on site
reach.learn: Scenario testing and practical route constraints

evidence.claim: Source-bound revision drafting and native contact-table assembly are feasible design components; the emergency-plan workflow and timings are model knowledge.

assumptions: Boundary is an actual emergency-plan revision and its existing internal distribution, not live emergency command. No response instruction is selected by the model.

Site personnel supply changes and current response-role contacts during s2; the specialist records changes and verifies role, name, phone, location and coverage in s3. The existing plan owner supplies the distribution list. Missing contacts require manual confirmation within retained s2-s3; there is no free clean contact feed.

Of twenty-nine revision hours, 11.6 are first prose assembly and 17.4 remain for rewriting; all twenty final review hours remain. Five contact-table hours concern repeated rows, not saving the document. Native templates are tested first.

Ordinary author saving remains within document work without a separate gate or benefit. The one-hour actual email distribution is distinct. This branch assumes the specialist has final distribution authority; any additional local plan-owner sign-off is retained and must be priced before use. Changes after s6 void release permission.
unknowns: Actual plan revision and distribution workflow
Contact-list quality and real table copying time
research_questions: Does the revised procedure preserve every operational constraint after full specialist correction?

already_counted.description: Rewrite site-specific instructions and check final operational meaning

incremental.description: Maintain revision restrictions, templates and distribution mappings

approvals.approved_version: s6 exact final plan text, contact table, revision identifier, attached file and named internal email recipient list; edits void permission

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central gross is 11.6 prose hours plus five contact-table hours plus one actual distribution hour, less two upkeep = 15.6. Cautious case: a materially changed emergency scenario requires all twenty-nine revision hours manually; verified contact assembly and actual distribution still remove six, less two upkeep = 4.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Confirm hazardous substances, work locations and affected worker groups
Review current safety data sheets and required substance information
Write the actual worker information pack and session notice
Check the final hazard information, session notice and recipient groups
Send the checked information and session notice to the named worker groups
Explain substance hazards, coordinate access to information and answer workers' questions

tasks.design: Configure a {DOCS} information template from specialist-selected safety data sheet sections and agreed session details. Keep source review and explanation human, and send only the exact checked package through {EMAIL}; no model selects hazard controls.
tasks.previous_blocker: Source selection, practical explanation and repeated information-pack formatting were intertwined.
tasks.enabler_now: Native document templates can reuse selected source blocks and session fields without interpreting hazards.
tasks.still_hard: Workers need information that fits actual exposure and can be understood in practice.
tasks.human_edge: The specialist answers questions and checks whether the safety information makes sense at work.
tasks.altitude: Some repeated pack assembly and the actual email send fall away; hazard interpretation and worker discussion stay.

reach.task: Check workers' access to substance information
reach.learn: Information usability and source revision control

evidence.claim: Native templates can assemble selected information blocks without choosing hazard controls; this role-specific design and saving estimate are model knowledge.

assumptions: Boundary is an actual hazardous-substance information program using an existing information pack and session notice. This is a functional description, not a claim that one named national right-to-know rule applies across Europe.

Workplace owners supply substance, location and affected work groups in the existing inventory. Suppliers provide safety data sheets. The specialist verifies and selects source sections in s1-s2; s3 includes first capture of selected text and session details agreed with the group coordinator. Missing inventory or source fields are manually resolved in those retained steps.

Only five of twenty pack-writing hours are repeated layout and fixed session fields; fifteen remain for first capture, practical explanation and tailored text. All nine final meaning-check hours and all thirty session hours remain. Native templates precede custom code.

Ordinary document saving is retained within s3. A real one-hour internal email send is separate and gated on the finished package and exact recipients. No attendance record, completion certificate or unperformed trailing log is added.
research_questions: Which information blocks can be reused without changing hazard meaning?

already_counted.description: Check final hazard meaning, notice details and recipients

incremental.description: Maintain information templates and recipient mappings

approvals.approved_version: s4 final exact information pack, source versions, session notice, attachments and named affected-worker email groups; changes void approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central gross is five repeated layout/field hours plus one actual send hour, less one upkeep = 5. Cautious case: a multilingual or unfamiliar-substance pack needs all twenty writing hours manually; only the real send removes one, offset by one upkeep, giving zero. Source review and discussion are unchanged.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Inspect hazardous waste handling and actual industrial site conditions
Question site personnel about processes, controls and observed discrepancies
Perform required site measurements or sampling and assess their limitations
Capture actual observations, interviews and measurements in the audit notes
Write audit findings and link them to actual evidence
Check each finding's meaning, evidence and stated uncertainty
Save the audit findings in the same document store

tasks.design: Use a native finding template in {DOCS} to reuse evidence identifiers and standard finding structure. All site inspection, interviews, sampling, first evidence capture and finding judgement remain with the specialist; the ordinary author save is unchanged.
tasks.previous_blocker: Audit evidence is varied, while only finding structure and evidence references repeat.
tasks.enabler_now: A configured document template can remove repeat structure without judging compliance.
tasks.still_hard: Incomplete samples and conflicting accounts require investigation rather than text automation.
tasks.human_edge: The specialist distinguishes evidence of a hazard from an unverified suspicion.
tasks.altitude: A modest writing reduction; site work and conclusions keep their full responsibility.

evidence.claim: Templates can reuse finding structure and evidence references; the audit-specific allocation is model knowledge, not measured safety improvement.

assumptions: Boundary includes real audit findings used in the investigation, not a newly invented progress log. Delivery of a separately commissioned final report is not claimed as automated here; any actual send needs separate measurement and a final-version gate.

The specialist supplies observation, interview, location, time, sample identifier, result, units and uncertainty in fully retained s4. Source criteria come from the audit scope owner. Missing facts or disputed evidence require manual investigation in unchanged s1-s4, not a clean extraction feed.

Three of fifteen finding-writing hours are repeat headings, evidence-reference formatting and copied identifiers; twelve remain for first finding composition, judgement and correction. All four final meaning-check hours remain. Use native templates first; the one-hour ordinary save is fully retained and ungated.
unknowns: Whether a separate report send is part of the local commission
research_questions: Does the present finding template already reuse evidence identifiers?

already_counted.description: Check finding meaning and evidence support

incremental.description: Maintain finding structure and evidence-reference fields

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central gross is three formatting/reference hours less 0.5 upkeep = 2.5. Cautious case: a one-off investigation has no reusable finding structure, or current templates already do this; retain all fifteen writing hours and deploy no extra template, giving zero. Site work and first capture receive no cut.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Develop and maintain employee medical monitoring programs

steps.what: Review work exposures, process changes and existing monitoring program scope
Discuss appropriate medical monitoring arrangements with the occupational health professional
Choose administrative responsibilities, review dates and permitted program information
Write or update the actual medical monitoring program document
Verify program meaning, responsibilities and consistency with professional advice
Save the updated program in the same document store

tasks.design: Configure a {DOCS} program template for the specialist's selected responsibilities and review dates. Keep exposure review, occupational-health consultation, scope choices, first program writing and meaning checks human; no individual medical result or clinical decision is generated.
tasks.previous_blocker: Program design depends on professional advice, although some document structure repeats.
tasks.enabler_now: A native template can reuse selected administrative fields without extending medical access.
tasks.still_hard: Appropriate monitoring scope and boundaries depend on exposure and qualified clinical advice.
tasks.human_edge: The specialist connects workplace exposure controls with the occupational health professional's recommendations.
tasks.altitude: Slightly less repeated document structure; no clinical decision rights or medical access are gained.

reach.task: Agree a workplace monitoring program boundary
reach.learn: Exposure context and separation of clinical and employer information

evidence.claim: Native program templates may reduce repeated administrative document assembly while leaving clinical advice human; the design and timing are model knowledge.

assumptions: Boundary is developing or maintaining the actual program document, not running examinations or sending invitations. Consultation time is the specialist's participation only; no physician labour is counted as saved.

Exposure assessment owners supply process, exposure category and affected work groups. The occupational health professional supplies appropriate monitoring advice. The specialist first records selected scope, owners, dates and permitted administrative fields in retained s3-s4; absent or unclear advice requires manual clarification, not an assumed clean health-data feed.

Three of twenty document hours are repeat headings and administrative table layout; seventeen remain for first capture, wording, case-specific arrangements and checking. All fourteen final meaning-check hours remain. Test native templates first.

No individual medical findings, sickness causes or model-generated clinical schedules enter the employer document. Local information boundaries and any separate adoption authority need confirmation. Ordinary same-system save is one hour fully retained and ungated; no program activation or external send is automated.
unknowns: Actual program template and clinical advice workflow
Local division of responsibilities and adoption authority
research_questions: Which existing program fields can be reused without copying clinical information into employer records?

already_counted.description: Verify program scope and consistency with professional advice

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central gross is three repeated structure hours less 0.6 upkeep = 2.4. Cautious case: a new exposure needs a bespoke program document or the current template already removes layout work; retain all twenty writing hours and deploy no extra template, giving zero. Consultation and program judgement remain unchanged.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The specialist retains site investigation, hazard interpretation, emergency design and medical-program coordination. Actual document assembly and narrowly scoped distribution are separate candidates for reduction.
reach: Work with safety technicians on evidence quality and with occupational health professionals on monitoring boundaries
skills_to_grow: Verify operational meaning in procedure revisions
Separate clinical advice from employer administration
role.ambitious_version: A safety specialist supported by clearer document handling while keeping site reality, worker understanding and qualified advice central.
